newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady-up, pork bellies steady-lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady-up, pork bellies steady-lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb higher while pork bellies were called steady to 0.150 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Mostly steady to higher cash hog indications and a late paring of losses Friday were expected to support hog futures early. However, a week tone to cash pork products will limit upside potential, analysts said.
Japan again said it is monitoring domestic pork prices and may cut the tariff rate on pork imports if necessary, which should underpin futures somewhat, analysts said.

Pork belly futures were seen showing carryover pressure on an easier tone to cash pork prices. Cash belly prices again turned toppy after reaching the $75 per cwt level. Analysts also noted that bellies will not benefit as much from the Taiwan pork ban as other pork cuts will likely benefit, they said.
But losses in futures will be limited by a lack of a hedge in futures which would keep storings light, they said.
The new fresh pork belly settlement price was quoted at $72.32, up $0.70 per cwt.
